_measurement: Cut from a real run: live Gemini (preflight provider=google), 7 scenarios x 5 repeats = 35 mission runs, against a dedicated oddjob_evals database.
_caveat: The capability subjects are NOT valid capability measurements yet. Each scores on tool_used (weight 3) + final_output_contains (weight 1); the tool was never called on any repeat, hence the flat 0.25 and zero variance. Across all 42 runs the orchestrator only ever selected browse_web, get_blackboard, google_search, http_request, python, think_step and update_blackboard. Two of the five scenarios also named tools that do not exist — write_file (the registered name is file_write) and save_to_dataset (a job type, not a capability) — so those two could never have scored regardless of what the orchestrator chose; they are corrected now, and tests/evals/scenario-tools.test.ts keeps them honest. Their old subject keys are removed rather than carried over with invented numbers, so capability:file_write and capability:add_dataset_items fall to defaultThreshold until someone re-cuts against a real run. The remaining three numbers describe what the harness currently does, not what the platform can do.
